title: Sequences — 12 machine-checked theorems and how they are bound
description:
Sequences. 12 machine-checked theorems from the Lean 4 source file src/proof/sequences.lean, by Tsvetan Rouschev, licensed CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Lean 4 is a proof checker: a theorem it accepts has been checked by its kernel, not argued in prose. All are checked case by case over a stated finite domain (by decide). Every theorem listed is sealed live in the deposit's ledger, where a withdrawal is marked in place; 63 earlier rows removed on 2026-08-09 are listed in src/proof/revoked.json.

How these theorems are bound. "Entangled" is used here in a precise, non-quantum sense: theorems are bound when they derive from shared definitions (section 1), when their files import one another (section 2), and when their content-addressed receipts fold into one address that changes if any one of them changes (section 3). It is correlation by derivation; no information travels through it.

1 · Shared definitions. 4 definitions are used by two or more theorems, binding 13 pairs; the theorems fall into 5 strands, the largest of 5. Most binding: fib (5), choose (2), tm (2), popcount (2). 1 theorem names no definition of the file and stands on its own statement.

2 · Imports. Built on: fnv.lean. Built on it: demand.lean, demand3.lean. Checking this cluster needs 2 files: src/proof/sequences.lean, src/proof/fnv.lean.

3 · The joint address. The 12 sealed receipts fold to 7850badf-1d06-819a-a625-34cc65765e57. Order-invariant: yes — the same root in reverse order. Altering one receipt changes it: yes, computed when this record was generated. A content-address proves integrity, not truth.

4 · The address lattice. Each theorem sits at the seven ray values its page plots from its receipt, taken mod 9: a point of (ℤ/9)⁷. This cluster's centre is (0, 1, 2, 3, 2, 3, 6). Its nearest clusters, ranked by lift — pairs counted from this cluster's theorems' seven nearest points, over the pairs expected by chance from the two clusters' sizes: rights.lean (3 observed, 1.02 expected, lift 2.94), priorart.lean (3 observed, 1.15 expected, lift 2.61), address.lean (4 observed, 2.17 expected, lift 1.84). A best lift is the largest of about 32 small ratios, so chance alone gives a typical best lift of 2.94 here (the median over 200 seeded reshufflings of which cluster each point belongs to); one at least as high as this cluster's arose in 63.0% of them — consistent with chance. Mean distance between two of its theorems: 14.61; from one of its theorems to a theorem of another cluster: 15.42. A receipt is a hash, so nearness on this lattice is a property of the addresses, not of the mathematics; the mathematical binding is (1) and (2). These figures are as of commit 83213ac8f1ad (2026-09-15), over 659 points; a new seal anywhere moves them.

Prior art. Cassini’s identity — G. D. Cassini, 1680; Lucas sequences — Édouard Lucas, 1878; the Brahmagupta–Fibonacci identity — Brahmagupta, 628; Pascal’s triangle mod 2 — Blaise Pascal, 1654. Per-theorem prior-art searches — OEIS, zbMATH Open, OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv — are recorded, with what was searched, where and when, in the living ledger src/proof/novelty.json (main branch). No novelty is claimed here.

The theorems.

  1. cassini_at_even_indices — (List.range' 1 20).all (fun n => n % 2 == 1 || fib (n - 1) * fib (n + 1) == fib n * fib n + 1) record
  2. cassini_at_odd_indices — (List.range' 1 20).all (fun n => n % 2 == 0 || fib (n - 1) * fib (n + 1) + 1 == fib n * fib n) record
  3. cassini_deviation_is_exactly_one — (List.range' 1 20).all (fun n => (fib (n - 1) * fib (n + 1) == fib n * fib n + 1) || (fib (n - 1) * fib (n + 1) + 1 == fib n * fib n)) record
  4. lucas_mod_two_is_the_and_rule — (List.range 14).all (fun n => (List.range (n + 1)).all (fun k => (choose n k % 2 == 1) == (andN k n == k))) record
  5. pascal_has_both_parities — ((List.range 14).flatMap (fun n => (List.range (n + 1)).map (fun k => choose n k % 2))).contains 1 ∧ ((List.range 14).flatMap (fun n => (List.range (n + 1)).map (fun k => choose n k % 2))).contains 0 record
  6. sums_of_two_squares_are_closed — (List.range 8).all (fun a => (List.range 8).all (fun b => (List.range 8).all (fun c => (List.range 8).all (fun d => (a*a + b*b) * (c*c + d*d) == (a*c - b*d) * (a*c - b*d) + (a*d + b*c) * (a*d + b*c) || (a*c) < (b*d))))) record
  7. three_five_eight_are_consecutive — fib 4 = 3 ∧ fib 5 = 5 ∧ fib 6 = 8 ∧ fib 4 + fib 5 = fib 6 record
  8. pisano_twentyfour_is_four_sixes — (List.range 30).all (fun k => fib k % 9 == fib (k + 24) % 9) ∧ 24 = 4 * 6 record
  9. thue_morse_doubling_recurrence — (List.range 200).all (fun n => tm (2 * n) == tm n && tm (2 * n + 1) == 1 - tm n) record
  10. doubling_preserves_the_parity_of_the_bits — (List.range 200).all (fun n => popcount (2 * n) == popcount n) record
  11. the_odd_step_sets_exactly_one_further_bit — (List.range 200).all (fun n => popcount (2 * n + 1) == popcount n + 1) record
  12. the_sequence_takes_both_values — ((List.range 200).filter (fun n => tm n == 0)).length = 100 ∧ ((List.range 200).filter (fun n => tm n == 1)).length = 100 record
